items.title: Viral podcast recounts 2016 drug trafficking case, says KL police chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The drug trafficking case near a place of worship close to the Sentul district police headquarters, recounted in the @Sembangohhyeahh podcast, dates back to 2016. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said three police reports were lodged in connection with the case on July 12, 2016. Fadil said police detected a video from the podcast that went viral this morning.

items.title: Melaka polls: PH candidates must build strong campaign machinery - Ramanan
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates contesting the Nov 14 Melaka state election must build strong campaign machinery rather than rely solely on their track records in serving the community to win voter support, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. He said a strong record in looking after the people's welfare would not be enough if candidates lacked a capable team to mobilise an effective campaign. "This is my personal view: candidates need strong campaign machinery.

items.title: Flood relief centres shut in Penang, Pahang and Kedah, Perak keeps two open
items.summary: In PAHANG, two PPS in Raub housing 26 evacuees from 11 families were also closed at 1pm today. However, the Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said two PPS remained in operation as of 4pm, at SK Matang Gelugor and SK Matang. The floods hit Kampung Matang Pasir and Kampung Matang Gelugor, while the storm also struck Kampung Changkat Baru Matang, Kampung Teluk Kertam, Kampung Melawati and Kampung Hujung Matang.

items.title: Sultan Sharafuddin's 25-year reign reflects deep concern for people's welfare, unity
items.summary: KLANG: The 25-year reign of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has been marked by his concern for the welfare of his subjects, the interests of Islam and harmony among the state's multi-ethnic communities. They said His Royal Highness's attentiveness to the concerns of the people was an important foundation for safeguarding their well-being and strengthening unity in the state. [[nid:1558387]] Bagan Nira village head Mohamad Sedek Idrus said Sultan Sharafuddin's firm stance on state issues, particularly those concerning Islam, reflected his commitment to fulfilling his responsibilities as ruler.

items.title: Public Service Dept says Hybrid Workday policy can be used to adapt to haze conditions
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 18 — Department heads in the public service sector can leverage the Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy to adapt to haze conditions in their respective states. Public Service Department (PSD) director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said that department heads may employ appropriate methods under the HBH framework to ensure that work deliverables or Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for every civil servant are met. Also present was the Terengganu Federal Development Department director Datuk Abdul Kahar Abdul Latif.

items.title: Umno Youth pledges mature, healthy conduct in Melaka polls
items.summary: Its election director, Mohd Hairi Mad Shah, said the party would adopt a positive campaigning approach. He said the youth campaign machinery would highlight BN's record in government from 1957 to 2018. Mohd Hairi, who is also Umno Youth deputy chief, said the party's youth machinery across all 191 divisions nationwide would be mobilised to support the Melaka election campaign.

items.title: Civil servants in haze-affected states can opt for hybrid WFH arrangement
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Civil servants working in states affected by the transboundary haze may carry out their duties under the Hybrid Working Day (HBH) policy. Public Service Department director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the haze problem coincided with the government's introduction of the HBH policy, which came into effect on Aug 1. He said department heads, particularly in states affected by haze, were allowed to implement the HBH arrangement.

items.title: Masidi: RM18.7b Sabah allocation covers civil service salaries, not just projects
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — The RM18.7 billion allocated to Sabah under Budget 2027 is not solely for development projects, but also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments in the state, Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun said. He said a large portion of the allocation will cover operating expenses, including salaries for about 120,000 federal civil servants working in Sabah. We need to understand that the allocation also covers the operating costs of federal ministries and departments operating in Sabah.

items.title: Negri MB on Tuanku Muhriz's rebuke: 'There's nothing to comment'
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declined to elaborate on the viral video which showed Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, having a stern word with him at a Kuala Pilah mosque last Friday. A video showing Tuanku Muhriz having a stern word with Ismail amid the state's constitutional crisis went viral last week. Ismail is seen in the clip acknowledging Tuanku Muhriz and paying homage to the ruler.

items.title: Undi18, automatic voter registration a challenge for BN in Melaka polls
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: The implementation of 'Undi18' and the automatic voter registration system pose a challenge for Barisan Nasional (BN) in the upcoming Melaka state election, which will take place next month. The Melaka BN chairman noted that although the coalition secured a resounding victory in the 2021 Melaka state election, this success could not be replicated during the 15th general election (GE15), where the coalition lost all six parliamentary seats. In the 2021 Melaka state election, BN won 21 out of the 28 contested seats, enabling it to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured two.

items.title: Melaka election to see wider use of OCR‑VA system, Election Commission confident after MCMC tests
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Election Commission (EC) have conducted internet connectivity checks at polling centres to test the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system ahead of the Melaka state election, which will take place next month. State Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications Committee chairman Datuk Fairul Nizam Roslan said one polling centre, Dewan Penyayang at the Lesung Batu Welfare Complex, was found to be unsuitable for the OCR-VA system due to unsatisfactory internet connectivity. Fairul Nizam said MCMC had also submitted a full report to the EC on internet connectivity at the polling centres to facilitate arrangements on election day.

items.title: Cat Stevens offers comfort to grieving Dr Mahathir
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A visit by legendary singer-songwriter Yusuf Islam, better known as Cat Stevens, to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali , has touched Malaysians, with many praising the musician for offering comfort during a difficult time. Yusuf shared that he had visited Dr Mahathir, whose wife died recently after 70 years of marriage. "Today I visited Dr Mahathir Mohamad, former prime minister of Malaysia, whose wife, Dr Hasmah, just passed away and read Al-Fatihah.

items.title: 2 held in Rawang subsidised diesel bust
items.summary: RAWANG: Two men were arrested after authorities seized 11,900 litres of subsidised diesel allegedly diverted through the misuse of fleet cards at an illegal storage facility in Rawang. Muhamad Hanif said investigations found that the syndicate bought subsidised diesel at nearby petrol stations using fleet cards under the Subsidised Diesel Control System 2.0 before transferring it to buyers. He said drivers bought subsidised diesel at several nearby petrol stations using fleet cards and transferred it directly into buyers' lorries.

items.title: MCMC, EC test internet connectivity at Melaka polling centres for OCR-VA system
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Election Commission (EC) have conducted internet connectivity checks at polling centres to test the Optical Character Recognition-Voter Attendance (OCR-VA) system ahead of the Melaka state election, which will take place next month. State Science, Technology, Innovation and Digital Communications Committee chairman Datuk Fairul Nizam Roslan said one polling centre, Dewan Penyayang at the Lesung Batu Welfare Complex, was found to be unsuitable for the OCR-VA system due to unsatisfactory internet connectivity. Fairul Nizam said MCMC had also submitted a full report to the EC on internet connectivity at the polling centres to facilitate arrangements on election day.

items.title: Singer Yusuf Islam visits grieving Dr Mahathir, offers prayers for late Tun Dr Hasmah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — British singer songwriter Yusuf Islam, better known as Cat Stevens, paid a visit to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today, following the recent passing of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali. In a Facebook post, Yusuf said he read Al-Fatihah with Dr Mahathir, noting that the couple had been married for 70 years. The gesture drew warm responses from admirers, many thanking the musician for consoling Dr Mahathir in his grief.

items.title: Pejuang eyes up to 3 seats in Melaka polls
items.summary: IPOH: Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) is eyeing two to three seats in the upcoming Melaka state election. "Two or three seats would be enough. Mukhriz said Pejuang would campaign alongside its coalition partners.

items.title: Nurse dies after 4WD plunges into river in Ranau
items.summary: RANAU: A nurse died after the four-wheel-drive vehicle she was driving plunged about 30m into a river near Kampung Nalapak, along Jalan Ranau-Telupid. Ranau district police chief Superintendent Mursalin Mahmud said the victim was driving an Isuzu D-Max from Telupid when the vehicle hit the barrier on the left side of a bridge before plunging into the river. Earlier, seven firefighters and two fire engines from the Ranau Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the crash site.

items.title: Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang and Penang schools resume Oct 19, masks encouraged
items.summary: In SELANGOR, the State Education Department (JPN) said that outdoor activities are to be suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks. School administrators are required to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and pay special attention to high-risk students. In MELAKA, the State Education Department (JPN) said that school administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students.

items.title: Saudi landmark closes offices after repeated Houthi attacks
items.summary: RIYADH: Riyadh's Kingdom Centre skyscraper ordered remote working for office tenants on Sunday following repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The imposing, 99-storey landmark announced "mandatory" remote working until further notice. The Saudi coalition's decade-plus war with the Iran-backed Houthis has reignited during the US-Iran war, with regular attacks reported by both sides.

items.title: 11.4pct figure does not reflect actual progress of Sabah Pan Borneo Highway - Dr Joachim
items.summary: KUDAT: The 11.4 per cent completion rate for the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project highlighted in the recent Auditor-General's Report does not reflect the actual physical progress on the ground, says Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam. The Sabah Public Works Minister said the figure only measured the number of fully handed-over packages, which accounted for just four of the 35 packages under Phase 1 of the project. He said construction works continued to show positive progress, with eight packages spanning 179 kilometres (km) proposed to be opened to motorists in stages before the end of 2026.

items.title: GRS needs to priorities Sabah, coalition over personal interests - Hajiji
items.summary: KUDAT: All component parties of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) must prioritise the interests of Sabah and the coalition over personal or individual party interests, in order to strengthen the state's bargaining power at the federal level, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. The Sabah chief minister said the state's political leverage in negotiations at the federal level must be anchored in the internal cohesion of GRS, rather than being undermined by power struggles for positions or political egos. Also present were GRS deputy chairmen Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, Tan Sri Anifah Aman, Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah, Datuk Ewon Benedick, and Datuk Chin Su Phin, as well as GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.

items.title: MEF calls for study before mandatory RM2,500 graduate salary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called for a thorough study before the government makes a minimum starting salary for graduates mandatory. Its president, Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman, said salary requirements varied across industries depending on the skills and knowledge required for different professions. Syed Hussain said hiring decisions went beyond academic qualifications, with employers also assessing candidates' communication, teamwork, presentation and analytical skills.

items.title: Schools in Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang, Penang to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: In SELANGOR, the state Education Department said that outdoor activities are to be suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks. School administrators are required to continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and pay special attention to high-risk students. In MELAKA, the state Education Department said that school administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings provided by the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students.

items.title: Perak shuts all hiking trails in forest reserves from Nov 2 to Jan 17 due to monsoon season
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — All hiking trails and recreational activities within permanent forest reserves (HSK) in Perak will be closed to the public from November 2 to January 17 next year due to the monsoon season. Perak Forestry director Datuk Mohd Basri Abdul Manaf said the directive took into account current risk assessments and the weather outlook report issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). “All hiking trails and recreational activities within Perak’s HSK, including jungle trekking, four-wheel driving and cycling, are prohibited during this period,” he said in a notice posted on the Perak Forestry Department’s official website.

items.title: Tawau fire victims thank PM for contribution
items.summary: TAWAU: Victims of the fire at Batu 2, Jalan Apas, have expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the special assistance provided to help ease the burden on affected families. Mohd Azmi Mohd Asri, 24, said the contribution from the prime minister was deeply appreciated and reflected his concern for the tragedy that had befallen the villagers. I hope to receive government assistance to repair my fire-damaged home," he said when met at a special assistance presentation ceremony initiated by the prime minister and delivered by Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud today at the temporary evacuation centre at the Tawau Sports Complex multipurpose hall.

items.title: Nationwide haze surge pushes API past 150 in 26 areas, Pasir Gudang worst at 182
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — A total of 26 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of this afternoon, with Pasir Gudang, Johor, recording the highest reading at 182. All three monitoring areas in Melaka also recorded unhealthy readings: Bukit Rambai (166), Melaka City (158) and Alor Gajah (157). A total of 41 areas recorded moderate API readings, while one area recorded a good reading.

items.title: Oregon families grapple with explaining school shooting to children
items.summary: LIZ'S seven-year-old-nephew hasn't been able to sleep since a teenage shooter opened fire at his Oregon elementary school, killing three children and a teacher. Sixteen-year-old Griffin John II killed three children and a teacher in the same special needs class he previously attended, before a father who happened to be passing the school grabbed his own gun and killed the attacker, authorities said. Another student, a seven-year-old girl, and another teacher were wounded, but are in stable condition.

items.title: Pasir Gudang tops unhealthy air quality readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-six areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, with Pasir Gudang, Johor, registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 181. Seremban and Pengerang both recorded readings of 167, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka registered 166 and Batu Pahat recorded 165. Tangkak and Segamat recorded readings of 158 and 156 respectively.

items.title: Tighter border controls curb drug supplies into Kelantan, says police chief
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Drug supplies into Kelantan have dropped significantly despite a rise in drug-related cases, says state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. Yusoff said a new strategic approach to tackling the state's drug problem had been implemented since July 15, alongside sustained enforcement operations. NST, News, Malaysia News, Kelantan, drug trafficking, drug supply, drug cases, Mohd Yusoff Mamat, police enforcement, border controls, cross-border smuggling, drug abuse, student urine tests, National Anti-Drug Agency, Nada, drug prevention, Kuala Krai, UNODC © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Fahmi confirms Pakatan vetting complete, Melaka candidates to sign bond with RM10m penalty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has completed vetting candidates who will contest the 16th Melaka state election, including checks with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said PH will announce its candidates on Oct 24, once the selection process is finalised. In the previous state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 state seats contested, while PH secured five.

items.title: Police open two investigation papers on activist, refugee issue
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Police have opened two investigation papers following a viral issue involving a social media activist and the Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan, including a robbery case that led to the arrest of two Malaysian men. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cases were being investigated under Sections 341 and 268, and Section 395 of the Penal Code. He said two men had been arrested to assist in investigations into a robbery involving a member of the Rohingya refugee community.

items.title: HRD Corp approves RM37mil in training grants for Melaka
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: A total of 6,995 Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications were approved in Melaka, covering 39,489 training places with financial assistance totalling RM37.03 million. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said improvements to HRD Corp's implementation system had strengthened governance and transparency to ensure training opportunities could be used by the intended groups. Ramanan said 24,729 participants had received training, while 7,734 claims worth RM30.14 million had been approved in Melaka.

items.title: Police open two probes into viral issue involving activist and Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 18 — Police have opened two investigation papers following a viral issue involving a social media activist and the Myanmar refugee community in Kelantan, including a robbery case that led to the arrest of two local men. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the cases were being investigated under Sections 341 and 268, and Section 395 of the Penal Code. He said two local men had been arrested to assist in investigations into a robbery involving a member of the Rohingya refugee community.

items.title: PH completes vetting of Melaka election candidates, including MACC checks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan has completed candidate vetting for the 16th Melaka election, including checks with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said selected candidates will also be required to sign a party bond, with heavy fines imposed if they breach its terms. The communications minister said PH expects to field a mix of fresh faces and seasoned politicians, adding that the line-up also reflects changes in constituencies following negotiations among coalition partners.

items.title: Hajiji urges GRS parties to put Sabah first, warns against ego and power struggles
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — All component parties of Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) must prioritise the interests of Sabah and the coalition over personal or individual party interests, in order to strengthen the state’s bargaining power at the federal level, said its chairman, Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. The Chief Minister of Sabah said the state’s political leverage in negotiations at the federal level must be anchored in the internal cohesion of GRS, rather than being undermined by power struggles for positions or political egos. Also present were GRS deputy chairmen Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, Tan Sri Anifah Aman, Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah, Datuk Ewon Benedick, and Datuk Chin Su Phin, as well as GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.

items.title: MCMC probes Threads content suspected of insulting Negeri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 18 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negeri Sembilan. In a statement today, MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. As part of the investigation, MCMC recorded a statement from an individual at the Labu police station.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Najib’s house arrest conditions being finalised, but RM50m fine yet to be settled
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that the matter is being pursued following a letter from the Pardons Board secretariat, which allows the Malaysian Prisons Department to set conditions for the implementation of house arrest. “The Malaysian Prisons Department is in the final phase, currently drafting it. In the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat to the Malaysian Prisons Department, it is stated that the Malaysian Prisons Department can impose any conditions.

items.title: Fahmi condemns cyberbullying of UM student, urges victim to lodge reports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has condemned the bullying and threats directed at Universiti Malaya (UM) student Ummi Umairah Bakhit following views she expressed at a forum. He also urged all victims of cyberbullying to immediately lodge reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) immediately. Fahmi said users should not assume that online posts carried no consequences, including when accounts used were believed to be fake.

items.title: Fahmi condemns cyberbullying of UM student Ummi after she questioned Najib fine donations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has condemned the bullying and threats directed at Universiti Malaya (UM) student Ummi Umairah Bakhit following views she expressed at a forum. He also urged all victims of cyberbullying to immediately lodge reports with the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) immediately. Fahmi said users should not assume that online posts carried no consequences, including when accounts used were believed to be fake.

items.title: MCMC probes Threads content insulting Negri Sembilan royal institution
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into content uploaded on the social media platform Threads, suspected of containing insults against the royal institution of Negri Sembilan. MCMC said the content in question touches on issues concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. MCMC is also examining how the content was disseminated across social media platforms and will work with relevant enforcement agencies should other offences under existing laws warrant action.

items.title: 4 Indonesians jailed for using fake passport stamps
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Four Indonesians were sentenced to five months' jail each by the Sessions Court after pleading guilty to using fake stamps on their passports when entering Malaysia. All four pleaded guilty before judge Zulkpli Abdullah. They comprised 24 Indonesians, two Bangladeshis, two Myanmar nationals and one Vietnamese.

items.title: Kuching, Samarahan and Serian record unhealthy API readings as haze lingers over Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 18 — Kuching, Samarahan and Serian recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm today. According to the Natural Resource and Environment Board (NREB) website, Serian recorded the highest reading at 155, followed by Kuching 154 and Samarahan 148. Seventeen districts recorded moderate levels.

items.title: Nearly 11pct of screened Kelantan toddlers found stunted
items.summary: Kelantan Health Department director Dr Kasuadi Hussin said screenings conducted across 10 districts found that 9.8 per cent of the children were underweight, 10.9 per cent were stunted, 0.3 per cent were not fully immunised and 9.6 per cent had not received exclusive breastfeeding. Dr Kasuadi said being underweight could result from several factors, including insufficient food intake, calorie deficiency and unhealthy dietary habits, such as excessive consumption of junk food. "Children's health problems can be detected early through screenings.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Russia attacked Ukrainian energy sector 76 times in past week
items.summary: KYIV: Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors dozens of times in the week since US President Donald Trump announced a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday. Zelenskyy also predicted even more US sanctions relief. Zelenskyy said Trump's latest action emboldens Russian President Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Najib house arrest rules in final drafting stage
items.summary: BESUT: The Prisons Department is in the final stages of drafting rules and conditions for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said. He said the department, which is responsible for implementing Pardons Board decisions, had received a letter from the board's secretariat setting out the decision and related conditions. Saifuddin said the letter from the Pardons Board secretariat also stated that the Prisons Department could set any appropriate conditions.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya and 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the entire Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as selected areas in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Sarawak and Sabah. In Kelantan, the affected areas are Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang, while in Terengganu, they are Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang. In Pahang, the affected areas are Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, they are Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Sepang, Kuala Langat and Kuala Selangor.

items.title: Pakatan finalises Melaka seat allocation but no deal yet with other parties, says PKR sec-gen
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has yet to reach any concrete agreement on possible political cooperation with other parties for the November 14 Melaka state election. Datuk Fuziah Salleh, who is Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) secretary-general, said, however, that seat-allocation negotiations among its three component parties — PKR, DAP and Amanah — had been finalised. She said PH was expected to contest more than 20 state seats, with nine allocated to PKR.

items.title: HRD Corp training grant applications surge after system reforms, says Ramanan
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Oct 18 — The surge in Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) training grant applications reflects the positive impact of measures taken to streamline its implementation system, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan. It takes considerable time, and we thank the entire HRD Corp team for their dedication to carrying out these improvements,” he told reporters after attending the HRD Corp ‘Pocket Talk’ Roadshow: From Policy to the People here today. Also present was HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Aziz.

items.title: Hajiji recalls mother borrowing RM15 for exam fees as he vows poverty will not define Sabah children
items.summary: KUDAT, Oct 18 — Ensuring that poverty does not determine the fate of Sabah’s children or stand in the way of their progress has become a personal mission and commitment for Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Education is what can lift our children out of poverty. Driven by this commitment, he said he had ensured that the state government increased the allocation for the Sabah State Government Scholarship (BKNS) to RM155 million in 2026, up from RM55 million in 2021, to fund the education of students from underprivileged backgrounds.

items.title: Unesco status alone won’t save silat if youth turn away, says Perak MB
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (Unesco) recognition of silat as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity does not guarantee its survival if younger generations increasingly distance themselves from training, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said. “We may have a proud silat heritage, but if young people turn away from the training arena, fewer will truly master and appreciate the art,” he said. Saarani said Malaysia has more than 150 identified silat styles, with the martial art declared a National Heritage in 2009 before gaining Unesco recognition as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2019.

items.title: ‘We cannot sit back’: Malaysia offers aircraft to fight Indonesia forest fires despite dangerously poor visibility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysia cannot afford to stand by as raging forest fires in Indonesia send thick haze across the region, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said today, as the country offered to deploy helicopters and water-bombing aircraft to help contain the blazes. But Mohamad warned that dangerously poor visibility, reportedly below 50m in affected areas, could hamper aerial firefighting operations and put pilots at risk. Thick smoke was also preventing aircraft from operating safely.

items.title: Anwar approves RM30m to resurface 600 roads in Perak, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved a special allocation of RM30 million to resurface 600 roads in residential areas across Perak, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. “In conjunction with the Perak DAP Convention, I announced on behalf of the Prime Minister a special allocation of RM30 million for road resurfacing works in residential areas across the state. He said this while speaking at the 24th Perak DAP Annual Convention, officiated by DAP Secretary-General Anthony Loke here today.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to be tabled next year to regulate online transactions, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 18 — The E-Commerce Bill will be tabled in Parliament at the first meeting next year to strengthen the regulation of online transactions, said Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh. Fuziah said the Retail Access Programme, which combines training and business matching, has helped 1,862 entrepreneurs from 2023 to October this year. She said the programme comprised 38 training series and 21 business matching series, involving 103 local brands and 552 stock-keeping units (SKUs).

items.title: Perak maintains ban on outdoor school activities despite improving API readings, says exco
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 18 — Although Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at four monitoring stations in Perak have shown a decline, outdoor school activities remain prohibited due to the current haze situation. State Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said schools in the state were operating as usual, while teaching and learning activities must be conducted indoors. He said the ban covers outdoor activities, such as camping and sports, while motivational programmes must also be held indoors.

items.title: Foreign minister: Nepal seeks legal amendments to expedite death certificates for 54 Malaysians
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 18 — The Nepalese government is seeking to amend the country’s laws to expedite the issuance of death certificates for 54 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following floods and landslides that hit the country in August. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Nepal’s existing laws require a waiting period of up to three years before death certificates can be issued for individuals who remain unaccounted for after a disaster. He said the death certificates are necessary for the victims’ families to manage related affairs, including matters involving banks and insurance companies.

items.title: Tok Mat: N. Sembilan crisis won’t disrupt BN’s Melaka state election machinery
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 18 — The crisis in Negeri Sembilan is not expected to affect Barisan Nasional’s (BN) preparations for the Melaka state election next month, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said the key was to ensure that strategies drawn up by the party leadership were effectively implemented by its election machinery to secure victory, adding that good strategies not implemented will also cause plans to fail. In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats to form the state government, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won two.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Malaysians advised to postpone non-essential travel to France amid protests
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — Malaysians have been advised to consider postponing non-essential travel to France until the situation improves amid ongoing demonstrations in major cities across the country. The Embassy of Malaysia in Paris has issued an advisory urging Malaysians in France to exercise caution and remain vigilant. “While travel to France remains unrestricted, Malaysians are advised to consider postponing non-essential travel until the situation improves,” the ministry said.

items.title: DAP reps who fail performance targets risk losing candidacy in GE16, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 18 — DAP representatives must meet strict key performance indicators (KPIs) or risk losing their candidacy in the next general election (GE16), party secretary-general Anthony Loke said today. According to Berita Harian , Loke stressed that all DAP lawmakers must serve with integrity, discipline and commitment. Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming was also present at the event.

items.title: Authorities capture 12-foot crocodile at Teluk Nipah beach in Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 18 — A 12-foot crocodile was captured at Teluk Nipah beach in Buntal here last Thursday. The Civil Defence Force Kuching (APM Kuching), in a Facebook post, said its response team, together with personel from the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) and Nemo Hunter team, carried out the operation to capture the crocodile. Meanwhile, in his Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the capture followed a public report from a 55-year-old man.

items.title: Warisan leader: Tawau residents endure water disruptions of up to two weeks, urges govt to act
items.summary: TAWAU, Oct 18 — Residents in several areas here have been forced to endure prolonged water supply disruptions lasting up to two weeks, prompting calls for the state government and Sabah Water Department to take immediate and comprehensive action. He said residents in Bandar Sri Indah had reportedly experienced water supply disruptions for 10 days, while those in Batu Payung, Ranggu, Apas Permai and Taman Millennium had faced disruptions lasting up to two weeks. Residents should not have to endure days or even weeks without a reliable water supply,” he said.
